source.source: HYG v4.4 (Hipparcos-Yale-Gliese Database, D. Nash / astronexus)
source.epoch: ICRS/J2000 equinox; source astrometry primarily Hipparcos-2007 reduction, epoch J1991.25
source.sentinelDistDoc: dist == 100000.0 marks an unmeasurable/negative Hipparcos parallax; rows with it are dropped, not shipped.
source.hipSentinelDoc: hip == 0 means the row has no Hipparcos catalogue number.

galacticFrame.source: Hipparcos Catalogue vol. 1 §1.5.3 (ESA SP-1200, 1997); J2000 galactic frame constants shared by astropy and SOFA

panorama.title: The Milky Way panorama
panorama.longitudeConvention: l = 0 at the column centre, increasing leftward (sky seen from inside)
panorama.latitudeConvention: b = +90 at row 0, -90 at the last row

catalogRegistration.role: retained source record only; the photograph is registered astrometrically and owns visible stars

pointSourcePresentation.positionSource: licensed ESO photographic local maxima; no Google catalogue bytes
pointSourcePresentation.qualification: native fixed-size catalogue behavior collapsed into the prepared cubemap; point positions and colors remain ESO-derived

sky.qualification: source-photographed full sky sampled in ICRF through the J2000 galactic frame and the anchor-registered panorama; the scene registration carries the Bacchus pole and epoch; Solar System objects in the mosaic are capture artefacts; no Sun is baked into the cubemap
sky.sceneRegistrationChain: galactic -> ICRF (J2000 constants) -> body-fixed (IAU pole and prime meridian at the epoch) -> ecliptic presentation frame

analyticRadialFit.qualification: Least-squares fit to annular red-channel means from the bound native 128 by 128 Sun texture; fitted values only, no source pixels.

distanceScaling.qualification: The opaque photospheric core is projected from the IAU nominal solar radius and the object catalog's mean heliocentric distance. The retained glow profile remains a visual presentation; the distance is not epoch-specific.

provenance.source: Pinned JPL Horizons elements and the published radar-model pole; arbitrary display phase, not an absolute rotational ephemeris
provenance.qualification: Computed Bacchus Sun direction at 2026-09-03T00:00:00 TT, expressed in the ecliptic presentation frame (north up, Sun left at zero yaw) and in view space at the default camera pose.

controls.label: Shape
controls.description: The shared grid marks unavailable surface imagery on this radar model. This is the paper’s conservative single-lobe working model, not a uniquely resolved shape. Radar data cover about half a rotation, and the degree of bifurcation remains uncertain. The pole is uncertain by tens of degrees; the sidereal period is 15.0 ± 0.2 hours. No resolved optical surface map is supplied. Lighting uses the published pole and arbitrary display phase.
controls.title: Radar shape model
controls.summary: A radar model based on half a rotation. Its shape and pole are uncertain; gray grid: no surface imagery.

controls.label: Elevation
controls.description: False color shows radius at the nearest source-surface point minus a 0.315 km reference sphere. It includes global shape, not gravitational height or independent measured topography. Correspondence farther than 1 m is withheld. This is the paper’s conservative single-lobe working model, not a uniquely resolved shape. Radar data cover about half a rotation, and the degree of bifurcation remains uncertain. The pole is uncertain by tens of degrees; the sidereal period is 15.0 ± 0.2 hours. No resolved optical surface map is supplied.
controls.title: Shape-derived radial height
controls.summary: Radar-model height relative to a 315 m sphere. Half a rotation was observed; the shape is uncertain.
